title: Michael Fagan and the Invention of Formal Code Inspection (1970s)
explainer: Long before pull-request review tools existed, Michael Fagan developed a structured inspection process at IBM in the mid-1970s, with defined roles, moderators, and entry/exit criteria, aimed purely at finding defects rather than fixing them on the spot. Fagan's inspections are the direct ancestor of treating code review as a repeatable discipline rather than an informal favor between colleagues. The practice also helped demonstrate, with real data, that catching defects before testing is far cheaper than catching them afterward.
